entities.summary:
Marco Solari was a Swiss–Italian architect, engineer, and sculptor who made significant contributions to the development of Renaissance architecture. Born in the late 14th century, Solari was a member of the prestigious Solari family, known for their artistic and engineering prowess. He worked closely with the Medici family in Florence, creating elaborate sculptures and architectural designs that showcased his mastery of Renaissance style.

Solari's most notable works include the 'Moses' sculpture, which is considered a masterpiece of Renaissance art, and the 'Pala Solari', a large altarpiece that adorned the church of San Gimignano. His designs were characterized by their use of gold, marble, and other precious materials, and were often decorated with intricate carvings and sculptures.

Solari's legacy can be seen in the many architectural and artistic developments that followed his death in 1405. His work influenced architects such as Brunelleschi and Alberti, and his sculptures can still be seen in museums and churches throughout Europe today.

In his lifetime, Solari was celebrated for his artistic talents, and his work was sought after by the Medici family and other wealthy patrons. However, his legacy has been somewhat overshadowed by that of his more famous contemporaries, such as Leonardo da Vinci and Michelangelo.

Despite this, Solari's contributions to the development of Renaissance art and architecture remain significant, and his work continues to inspire artists and architects to this day.
